corrections.finding: Claim stronger than source: 'a group's route ... as its oldest bird is older' makes a measure (oldest bird's age in the group) the source lacks; source says learning from older birds reduced deviation from a straight line.
corrections.fixed_text: Whooping cranes from captive breeding, an ultralight aircraft leading their first migration, go on to migrate alone or in groups; over eight years, a crane's flying route keeps closer to a straight line as it learns from older birds, seven years of experience bringing a 38 percent improvement in accuracy, and genetic relatedness making no difference.

corrections.finding: Dissolved word and claim stronger than source: 'each thermal' (source says 'within thermals', not every one).
corrections.fixed_text: In a migrating flock of young white storks, leaders fly irregular paths, searching out the rising warm air within thermals, and followers soar in more regular paths on their exploring, losing height faster between thermals and flapping more; a bird's place in the flock goes with its flying efficiency, efficient fliers going on to winter in West Africa and less efficient ones in southern Europe, a winter place foreseeable from a few minutes of flight.

corrections.finding: Measure changed: 'migrate under 9 percent of the time' turns a share of animals (under 9% of translocated animals migrated) into a share of time.
corrections.fixed_text: Bighorn sheep that people move into ranges whose earlier herds are at an end: under 9 percent of them migrate, against 65 to 100 percent in herds that stay whole; herds starting again there take nearly 40 years to reach 80 percent migrating, and moose about 90 years, a herd's going with the spring's new growth up the slopes improving over decades, the knowledge passing from mothers and herd members to the young.

corrections.finding: Dead and dissolved words: 'were never lost' has 'never' (dissolved) and 'lost' (dead past participle); replaced with 'stay whole'.
